howToPlay: Press Start. After a short pause the ball is served from the middle of the court.
Your paddle is on the right. Move your mouse over the screen, or drag up and down with your finger, to move it.
Hit the ball back past the machine's paddle on the left to win a point. If the ball gets past you, the machine wins the point.
Hit the ball with the end of your paddle to send it off at a steep angle. A hit in the middle sends it straight back.
Every hit in a rally makes the ball a little faster.
The first to seven points wins the match.
controls: Mouse: move over the screen to move your paddle. Touch: drag up and down anywhere on the screen. Start begins a match, Restart begins a fresh one and Stop ends it. Start and Stop also work from the keyboard: press Tab to reach them, then Enter or Space.
computer: The machine's paddle chases the ball up and down, but it has a top speed, so it cannot always keep up. A fast ball sent off at a steep angle can get past it. It does not work out where the ball will end up. It only follows where the ball is right now. While it waits for a serve, it goes back to the middle.
notes: Ported from the original 1973 arcade source (UPD8-group/1973, src/components/TvTennis.jsx) with the same television, court, physics, speeds, machine player, tones and wording. What changed, and why: the captions use middle dots instead of dashes ('first to seven · drag on the screen to move', 'you win the channel · press start to defend it'). The site's status line also shows Press Start, the score while you play ('You 3, machine 2') and who won ('You win, 7 to 4' or 'The machine wins, 7 to 4'). Winning a match sets off the site's celebration (confetti, a fanfare and a toast), so the fanfare plays over the arcade's own point bleep. A loss keeps the arcade's own low buzz and does not add the site's lose sound, so the tones stay as they were. As in the original, the paddle follows the mouse or a finger and there are no keys for it. The screen has role img so screen readers read its description, and the play and stop symbols on the Start and Stop buttons are hidden from screen readers. The screen keeps the original fixed 640 by 440 drawing size, scaled to fit as in the original, so it looks exactly the same. The game already waits while the page is hidden, because browsers pause animation then. The section heading is not ported because the page gives the title. On phones the television can be a few pixels wider than in the original because this site's page margins are narrower.
